description:
Capture reads a declared contribution's value back from the repository's own
registries, so a contributed value an adopter changed in place is refreshed
from that change instead of wedging repository validation.

## Background

A profile contributes semantic values into the repository's declared
configuration. An adopter who changes one of those values in place reaches a
state no sanctioned sequence clears, verified against a built binary:

    jit profile validate  -> '.jit/config.toml:map-entry:type-hierarchy-types:widget'
                             no longer holds the value this profile published  (exit 4)
    jit validate          -> [profile-ownership] rule error; repository validation fails
    jit validate --fix    -> 0 fixes would be applied
    jit profile capture   -> manifest unchanged; contributions are not read
    jit profile apply     -> "unchanged"; the repository keeps the adopter's value
    jit profile reconfigure -> "unchanged"; identical outcome

Capture draws asset bytes from the repository for a live-source declaration, but
it reads no contribution at all, so the one class of profile-owned content whose
author is the repository is the one class capture cannot refresh. That inverts
the ownership the charter states: a record is provenance and ownership evidence
and never an authority for declared repository configuration (`@/charter/D-8`
decision D-04 on this container), yet here the record's copy outranks the
registry in every available operation while none of them can reconcile the two.

The other classes need no equivalent work, and this issue must not add it. A
managed region's body is generated from the package's region source, and an
install-only asset's bytes are content the package authors rather than content
the repository holds, so neither has a repository-side value to read back; an
apply re-renders the region, and an edited install-only asset is refused with an
actionable conflict that names restoring the published value.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Capture refreshes every contribution the manifest declares from the value the repository's registries currently hold, so a contributed value changed in place becomes the package's declared value.
- [hard] REQ-02: Capture reads only the contributions the manifest already declares and infers no new contribution from repository state, so a package cannot widen through capture.
- [hard] REQ-03: After a capture and a re-application, a repository whose contributed value was changed in place reports agreement from both the profile check and whole-repository validation.
- [hard] REQ-04: A declared contribution whose target the repository no longer holds is reported by name rather than dropped from the captured manifest or replaced by a default.
- [hard] REQ-05: Capture republishes the manifest whole, so a contribution the manifest stopped declaring does not survive in the captured package.

## Notes

The manifest is already republished by capture as an ordinary declared source,
so the contribution values reach the captured tree through that same manifest
rather than through a second write path.
title: Refresh declared contributions from the repository on capture
